title: Add compact presubmit scaffold and 'dep-sculptor' dependency pruner to speed CI feedback
author: Priya Anand
description: Context: CI feedback latency has been a recurring friction point for feature development. Large monolithic presubmit runners and a noisy dev dependency surface are the two main contributors. Motivation: provide a compact presubmit scaffold that runs a lightweight verification path for quick feedback and a new 'dep-sculptor' tool to trim transient devdeps used only by long-lived jobs, reducing install time and improving cache reuse. Goals: 1) Reduce median presubmit setup time by ~30%, 2) Keep full integration tests run on nightly/merge lanes, 3) Make dependency pruning opt-in per-package and auditable. Changes in this PR: - Add compact presubmit scaffold (pkg/ci/scaffold) that detects changed paths and runs a slim task set (lint-fast, unit-fast, typecheck-fast). - Introduce dep-sculptor: a small Go-based CLI (tools/dep-sculptor) that analyzes lockfile usage, builds a candidate prune set, and emits an audit-friendly plan. - Wire opt-in presubmit profile in .github/ci-profiles.yml and update workflow composite actions to select the fast path when profile matches. - Add a presubmit-local-runner script to speed up local iteration and warm the remote cache. - Add telemetry (metrics/ci) for presubmit duration, install time, and dep-sculptor prune size. Rollout plan: staged rollout via feature flag in CI config (default off), small opt-in on engineering teams, full enable when metrics show stable pass rates. Checklist: - [x] Add compact scaffold implementation and tests - [x] Add dep-sculptor prototype + unit tests - [x] Update workflows to support profile selection - [x] Add docs: docs/ci/compact-presubmit.md - [x] Add Linear links and feature flag gating - [x] Run dogfood on redwood repo and validate flakes/false-positives Notes: dep-sculptor is conservative by default: it records an audit plan but does not alter lockfiles unless --apply is specified. We ran a 2-week dogfood window on a subset of repos and saw median install times drop ~28% and cache hit rates improve. See release_notes for rollout guidance and opt-out instructions.

release_notes: Add compact presubmit scaffold (opt-in) and dep-sculptor dependency pruning tool. Opt-in via .github/ci-profiles.yml. Default behavior is safe (dry-run audit). To enable aggressive pruning, run tools/dep-sculptor --apply with an audit review. See docs/ci/compact-presubmit.md for migration steps and opt-out instructions.
notes: Dogfooded on subset of org repos for 14 days. Observed ~28% median install time improvement and fewer cache misses for presubmit lanes. No increase in presubmit flakes detected. Team will monitor telemetry for two weeks post-merge.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: overly aggressive pruning could remove devdeps required by rare integration paths. Mitigation: default dry-run, feature-flag rollout, artifacts and metrics for audit, and an easy revert workflow included in the docs.
manual_steps: To enable aggressive pruning: 1) Run tools/dep-sculptor --plan -o plan.json 2) Review plan.json artifacts in CI 3) Run tools/dep-sculptor --apply with branch and PR to update lockfile 4) Open a PR and run full integration checks
notes_for_oncall: If presubmit run times increase after rollout, toggle feature flag in .github/workflows/presubmit.yml to revert to legacy path. Dep-sculptor failures are non-blocking (dry-run) unless explicitly applied.
auditing: All dep-sculptor plans uploaded as CI artifacts named dep-sculptor-plan-<run-id>.json. Metrics exposed: ci.presubmit.duration_ms, ci.install.time_ms, ci.dep_sculptor.prune_count, ci.dep_sculptor.applied_count.
